assessment.where_you_stand: Your landlord in Noida is refusing to return your security deposit of Rs 40,000 [KB:deposit_civil_route], and you face a serious issue because the landlord's son reportedly pushed and threatened you. Since physical threats and violence are involved, this has crossed from a simple civil rental dispute into a potential criminal matter. Your strength is that security deposits must generally be refunded upon handing back possession [KB:src_mta_2021_11], but your weakness right now is the lack of written proof and the safety risk posed by threats. You must handle the safety aspect with priority.

options.title: Consult a Lawyer / Legal Aid
options.what_to_do: Because there are threats and physical intimidation involved, speak to a lawyer or approach the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for guidance before taking any further action.
options.cost: Free via DLSA or nominal consultation fee

options.title: Report Threats to Police
options.what_to_do: If you have been physically threatened or pushed, consider filing a police complaint regarding the intimidation and assault for your personal safety.
needs: Details of the landlord and incident

options.title: Send a Written Demand Notice
options.what_to_do: Through a lawyer, send a formal written demand notice to the landlord for the return of your security deposit [KB:deposit_civil_route].

proof_tips: Gather any bank statements or UPI receipts showing the Rs 40,000 transfer to the landlord.
Save any WhatsApp chats, text messages, or call logs where the deposit or the dispute was discussed.
Write down a detailed timeline of when you vacated the premises and when the threats occurred.
what_i_dont_know: Whether you have a signed written rent agreement covering the exact terms of the deposit refund.
Whether Uttar Pradesh has formally implemented specific provisions of the Model Tenancy Act [KB:mta_s11_deposit] locally.
Whether there are any counter-claims or unpaid rent alleged by the landlord.
assessment.needs_lawyer_reason: A lawyer is needed because the situation involves physical threats, intimidation, and potential police/criminal angles rather than just a straightforward money recovery.
assessment.reply: Your situation is serious because it involves not just a disputed security deposit of Rs 40,000, but also physical threats and intimidation from the landlord's side. While tenants generally have a right to get their deposit back after handing over possession [KB:src_mta_2021_11], safety and criminal risks take priority. You should consult a lawyer or contact the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at helpline 15100 before taking further steps [KB:lsa_s12_legal_aid] [KB:deposit_civil_route].
